articles.title: A smart home gateway earns its place for three reasons, and none of them is range
articles.excerpt: Gateways are usually sold as coverage devices. The box promises to extend reach, blanket the property, and remove dead zones, which is a compelling pitch and mostly irrelevant to why the device is use…
articles.body: Gateways are usually sold as coverage devices. The box promises to extend reach, blanket the property, and remove dead zones, which is a compelling pitch and mostly irrelevant to why the device is useful. A gateway is not a range extender, and treating it as one leads to buying it at the wrong moment and expecting the wrong result. What it actually does is quieter and more structural: it decides where decisions get made. The gateway is not a Wi-Fi extender If your problem is that a camera at the far end of the property drops off the network, a gateway will not fix it. That is a radio problem between one device and one access point, and the fix is an access point, a better antenna, or a closer mounting position.
articles.author: Xingliao Smart Home

articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine. Have you ever received an official notice, university circular or application document and struggled t…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine . What I Built Have you ever received an official notice, university circular or application document and struggled to understand what you actually need to do? Sometimes the most important instructions are hidden inside lengthy paragraphs, scanned documents and complicated language. Deadlines get overlooked, required documents get missed, and important information gets lost. I built NoticeLens , a multimodal AI document companion that helps bring those hidden instructions back into view. The idea behind the Ghost in the Machine theme is that the ghosts aren't necessarily supernatural.

articles.title: UI Framework for Humans and AI Agents: 6 Platforms, 900 KB, Rust/C/C++/ASM
articles.excerpt: I've been working on uison, a lightweight UI framework in Rust, and wanted to share it: Tiny footprint: About 900 KB in size. Cross-platform: Runs on Windows (x64, ARM), macOS, Linux, Android, iOS/iPa…
articles.body: I've been working on uison, a lightweight UI framework in Rust, and wanted to share it: Tiny footprint: About 900 KB in size. Cross-platform: Runs on Windows (x64, ARM), macOS, Linux, Android, iOS/iPadOS, and WASM. Dual-mode rendering: Renders a graphical UI for humans or exposes the UI structure and actions via MCP (Model Context Protocol) as JSON, allowing AI agents to interact with it without screenshots. SSH UI Forwarding: Thanks to the JSON representation, you can easily pipe and forward the UI over SSH. Polyglot examples: Comes with usage examples in Rust, C, C++, and even ASM. uisonlab / uison A tiny (<900 KB) cross-platform Rust UI framework with C/C++/ASM bindings that compiles JSON layout diffs to native pixels, featuring MCP integration for AI agents and SSH UI forwarding.

articles.title: App Attest and Play Integrity won't catch a real phone behind a proxy
articles.excerpt: App Attest and Play Integrity answer one question: is this my genuine app on a genuine device? That's worth knowing, and you should use them. But a real, unmodified app on a real phone passes, whether…
articles.body: App Attest and Play Integrity answer one question: is this my genuine app on a genuine device? That's worth knowing, and you should use them. But a real, unmodified app on a real phone passes, whether that phone is on a home connection or behind a proxy in a rack of phones. So if you're fighting fake signups, bonus farming or account takeover, you need a second question: what network is this request coming from? Why not check on the device? You can look for a VPN from inside the app. On Android, NetworkCapabilities.hasTransport(TRANSPORT_VPN) tells you about a VPN on the device. It's fine for showing a message, but it won't help against fraud, for two reasons: The app is reporting on itself. A modified client can answer whatever it likes. It can't see a proxy further upstream.
articles.author: FindIP

articles.title: How to export multiple Confluence pages to Word
articles.excerpt: Short answer. Confluence Cloud has no built-in way to put several pages into one Word document. The Word export on a page exports that page only, and the space export offers PDF, HTML, XML and CSV but…
articles.body: Short answer. Confluence Cloud has no built-in way to put several pages into one Word document. The Word export on a page exports that page only, and the space export offers PDF, HTML, XML and CSV but not Word. The free route is to export the pages you need into one PDF (the space PDF export lets you pick them) and open that PDF in Word. If the document has to look right or is produced regularly, use an app that exports a page tree straight to Word. What Confluence does natively Word export: one page, no children Every page has an Export to Word option in its actions menu; the same export sits at /wiki/exportword?pageId= followed by the page ID. We tested it on a parent page with two child pages: the file contained the parent page and nothing from either child.
articles.author: Mikhail Klimenko

articles.title: Scrape Wikipedia in 4m♭ (four minutes flat)
articles.excerpt: I Process All of English Wikipedia in Under 4 Minutes After a one-time 25 GB download, every subsequent extraction — jazz musicians, sci-fi novels, literary authors, whatever you want — runs against a…
articles.body: I Process All of English Wikipedia in Under 4 Minutes After a one-time 25 GB download, every subsequent extraction — jazz musicians, sci-fi novels, literary authors, whatever you want — runs against all 25.8 million Wikipedia pages in about three and a half minutes. Here's how I got there. The goal Transform a corpus of semi-structured Wikipedia data into searchable, structured database tables as fast as possible . Background Previously, I've done data visualization projects with data scraped from Wikipedia pages. I used asynchronous, depth-first page crawling that extracted key data related to jazz music from artist, album, and genre pages. After fetching a page, a top-level switch classified each one as a jazz artist, jazz album, or jazz-related genre.

articles.title: I built ~70 tiny browser puzzle games with no framework, no accounts, and a 900-byte score system
articles.excerpt: Gamebreak is a new site of short browser puzzle games: open one between two tasks, finish in a few minutes, close it. No login wall, no account, no app install. It has around 70 games: Sudoku, Mahjong…
articles.body: Gamebreak is a new site of short browser puzzle games: open one between two tasks, finish in a few minutes, close it. No login wall, no account, no app install. It has around 70 games: Sudoku, Mahjong, FreeCell, 2048, a Tetris-style game, Hashi, Nonogram, Sokoban, a Wordle-style word game and more. Most rounds take 2–4 minutes. The audience is office workers and students taking short breaks. That one decision drove almost every technical choice below. No framework, one small script per game Each game page is plain, hand-written HTML with a handful of script tags. On the 2048 page , for example, the page loads: i18n.js – a tiny language helper (~3 KB) score.js – the score store (~0.9 KB) 2048.js – the game itself (~6 KB) share.js – result sharing ads.js – ad slot setup That's it.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .
articles.author: Anthony Wood

A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today (Oct. 31) at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT; 9:04 p.m. on Oct. 30 local time), sending 27 of the company's Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO). The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base just after midnight ET on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) It was the 18th flight for this particular booster, which is designated B1093.

articles.excerpt: "He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love."
articles.body: As we all begin to absorb the bitter news of Patrick Stewart's death at the age of 86, a flood of personal tributes are pouring in, reflecting this global treasure's wonderful life lived with a dignity and bravado that few mortals possess. We’re getting just a hint of what Patrick Stewart meant to those who worked with him or knew him throughout his stellar career. Whether on stage with the Royal Shakespeare Company, on TV as the dashing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in " Star Trek: The Next Generation ," and in Hollywood spectacles like 1984's "Dune," four " Star Trek " feature films, and the many "X-Men" movies in which he portrayed Professor Charles Xavier, Stewart was always the consummate professional. articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
